readings.title: Resurrection Gospel at Matins
readings.text: (7) Our Lord Jesus Christ, after that he was risen from the dead, speedily manifested himself to his Disciples. Wherefore the Church, by the reading of the Gospel after the Song of the Holy Women, announces to the People one of the ten Manifestations of the risen Saviour to his Disciples. The appointed Gospels for Matins in their order will be found on p. xxi. All the eleven Lessons from the Gospels, appointed to be read in rotation, refer to the Resurrection of our Lord on the third day. (8) While the Choir sings, the Priest and Deacon first salute the Holy Gospels. And after them the people, in the presence of the Priest, as it were of the Angel-Messenger of the Resurrection, joyfully do homage to the Holy Book, as to Christ himself, and kiss it, in that it contains the redeeming tidings of the Resurrection.

readings.title: First prayer at Matins
readings.text: O Lord our God, who hast raised us up from our beds, and hast put into our mouths the word of praise, that we may adore and call upon thy holy Name. And we entreat thee, by thy mercies which thou hast exercised always in our life, send down now also thine aid upon those who stand before the presence of thy holy glory, and await the rich mercy which is from thee. And grant that they may always with fear and love worship thee, praise thee, hymn thee, and adore thine inexpressible goodness. For unto thee is due all honour, glory and worship, to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now, and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

readings.title: Why does the Gospel book have a prominent place?

paragraphs.text: Hapgood explains the appointed resurrection Gospel readings as an announcement of the risen Christ’s appearances to his disciples. Her account of reverence for the Gospel book connects the physical book with the saving message it contains. These explanations describe the service-book tradition of this edition.

readings.title: What is expressed in the opening prayer of Matins?

paragraphs.text: The prayer gives thanks for being raised from sleep and enabled to offer praise. It asks for God’s help for those assembled in worship. Its morning setting connects the beginning of the day with the life of the worshipping community.
